source.label: thm:rate
source.quote: Let $\eq$ be the (necessarily unique) Nash equilibrium of a $\str$-strongly monotone game. If the players follow (MD-b) with Euclidean projections and parameters $\step_{\run} = \step/\run$ and $\mix_{\run} = \mix/\run^{1/3}$ with $\step > 1/(3\str)$ and $\mix>0$, we have $\exof{\norm{\est\act_{\run} - \eq}^{2}} = \bigoh(\run^{-1/3})$.

results.notes: Bound on expected squared distance of realized actions to Nash equilibrium, not regret. Restated as Theorem 9(b). Theorem 1 (a.s. convergence in monotone games, no rate) not recorded as it gives no bound.
